what: Kit's bubble states a false fact: that "Apple" would come after "apple" in default sort order. With default sort, capitals come first, so "Apple" sorts before "apple". Panel 41 then says the opposite ("Capital letters come before small ones, which is why "Apple" leads").

fix: Reword the bubble: "Is it broken? And why does "Apple" come before "banana", but "banana" would come after "Zebra"?" Or drop the second question. If the example is kept, add "Zebra" to words in sort_default.js and recapture so the claim is shown by a real run.

what: Wrong version facts. findLast is ES2023, not ES2022 (both proposals were published in 2023). And "Node versions before 20 do not [have them]" is true only for toSorted and toReversed: findLast already shipped in Node 18.
evidence: Page: "toSorted, toReversed and findLast are newer methods (ES2023 and ES2022), but both Node versions have them; very old browsers and Node versions before 20 do not." TC39 finished-proposals (github.com/tc39/proposals/blob/main/finished-proposals.md): "Array find from last" and "Change Array by copy" both list expected publication year 2023. Node 18 has findLast (V8 9.7+, per MDN compat data; I couldn't run it because no Node 18 is installed here).
fix: "toSorted, toReversed and findLast all arrived in ES2023. Both Node versions here have them; findLast needs Node 18 or later, and toSorted/toReversed need Node 20 or later."

what: The caret explanation is inaccurate. The ReferenceError comes from evaluating `typeof seat`, before console.log is called, so console.log was not "the call that was running". V8 just reports the position of the surrounding call expression.
evidence: Readlist: "V8, the engine inside Node, marks the call that was running when the error was thrown." tdz_typeof.js: stdout has only line 1's "undefined"; the error points at 2:9 (the `log` of console.log), with no console.log frame in the trace.
fix: "this time the caret sits under log, not under seat: V8 points at the call the bad read sits inside. Trust the message and the line number first; the caret is a hint."

what: One distractor's "why" text is not always true. A var declared and used only inside one function can still crash after a swap to let: when it's declared inside an if block and read after that block. That is the chapter's own "var walks through block walls" lesson.
evidence: Option "A variable declared and used only inside one function", why: "Safe. It stays in the function's room either way." Panel 28 var_block.js and verdict card v_var_block.js show var leaving a block. The same file with let (v_let_block.js) throws "ReferenceError: e is not defined".
fix: Narrow the option: "A variable declared at the top of a function and used only further down in it", with the why "Safe: every use comes after the declaration, in the same room."
